findings.title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
findings.body: The existing password check runs only when credentials.totpCode is falsy, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP validation. A caller can submit a valid backupCode together with any nonempty totpCode and an incorrect or missing password: password verification is skipped and the arbitrary TOTP is never checked. This allows possession of a backup code alone to authenticate a password-based account. Ensure the required primary credential is verified independently of which second-factor branch is selected.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
findings.body: Backup codes are read from the user record, checked in memory, and then overwritten with an unconditional update by user ID. Two concurrent login requests can both read the same unused code and both authenticate successfully. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes, restoring a code already consumed by the other request. Use an atomic conditional update (checking the previously stored value and rejecting or retrying on conflict) or transactional locking so that successful authentication guarantees the code was consumed exactly once.
